action: Resolve the worker194 continuation by comparing the pinned rust-sdk task gate with the official SEP-2663 capability-negotiation and polling text, specifically whether a caller-visible server-capability preflight is normatively required before tasks/get.
result: The official SEP-2663 task lifecycle defines capability negotiation as the client declaring io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks and the server advertising the same extension, followed by task creation and client polling via tasks/get. In the reviewed specification text, clients SHOULD respect pollIntervalMs, but no client MUST/SHOULD perform a separate ServerCapabilities::supports_tasks-style preflight immediately before tasks/get once a task handle has been returned. At modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk@4a738b9dd99eaca418b614afa433a0cbdaf8d056, server-side validate_tasks_capability gates tasks/* on the server's advertised tasks capability and the client's declared tasks capability, while worker194 already established that Peer<RoleClient>::get_task sends GetTaskRequest directly without such a caller-side preflight. Exact-scope conclusion: a caller-side server-capability check can be a defensive check for misconfiguration/nonconformance, but the reviewed normative flow does not make it a prerequisite for polling a returned task handle.
